channel.title: Orbi Blog
channel.description: Notes from shipping Orbi in the open: delivery runs, failures, fixes, and measurements.

item.title: Pi coding agent worktree: a failed recovery
item.description: A surviving branch stalled Orbi's queue after a failed run. How Pi sessions, worktrees and a stable branch help recover work before a pull request exists.

item.title: Aider vs OpenCode: context, commits and checks
item.description: Compare Aider vs OpenCode 2 by file context, Git commits, tests and permissions. Use the same starting commit to inspect what each agent actually changes.

item.title: OpenCode alternatives: who merges and releases?
item.description: OpenCode takes an Issue to an open PR and a review, then stops. The OpenCode alternatives below differ in who owns the merge and release after the PR.

item.title: Claude Code pricing: Pro, Max and API billing
item.description: Compare Claude Code pricing for Pro, Max and API access. Check shared limits, extra usage, API credit exclusions and which account pays before you upgrade.

item.title: Cursor vs Claude Code: workflow, plans and usage
item.description: Choose Cursor vs Claude Code by workflow, execution environment and billing. Compare current plans, Claude access and a simple task evaluation checklist.

item.title: Can an AI agent contribute to open source?
item.description: Orbi fixed issues in brig, LLMVault and pyinfra, and maintainers merged all three PRs. On pyinfra our automated review missed a bug and a human caught it.

item.title: Claude Code subagents setup and when to use them
item.description: Claude Code subagents handle delegated tasks in separate contexts. Configure a focused reviewer, give it clear inputs, and decide when delegation helps.

item.title: How to check and reset Codex usage limits
item.description: Codex usage limits use five-hour and weekly windows set by plan. Check them on the Usage page or with /status, see when they reset, and keep runs going.

item.title: Codex YOLO mode: what runs without approval
item.description: Codex YOLO mode skips approvals and the local sandbox. Linux tests show what it allows; the guide also explains Codex auto mode and the full-auto removal.

item.title: YOLO mode Claude Code vs auto mode: what I measured
item.description: YOLO mode in Claude Code is --dangerously-skip-permissions. I tested it against auto mode and the safer modes on 2.1.287: what runs, what stops injection.

item.title: New users waited 1–2 min; long polling made it 10 s
item.description: One new user left our preparing page after their workspace was already ready. Long polling and a handful of small fixes cut the wait to about 10 seconds.

item.title: Claude Code sandbox: what each setup blocks
item.description: Tested on Linux with --dangerously-skip-permissions: the default Claude Code sandbox let four escapes through; strict settings plus a deny rule held.

item.title: Ralph loop's code passed 28 tests, then failed review
item.description: A Ralph loop reruns one prompt. Mine wrote code that passed all 28 tests, including 13 it never saw, yet a separate review session found a spec violation.

item.title: Write a request: Orbi Cloud drafts your GitHub Issue
item.description: Write a request in Orbi Cloud: describe a change, review a GitHub Issue draft, answer open questions, and hand it off. See merge controls and trial costs.

item.title: Pi agent harness: CLI, AI SDK, Pi Durable vs kill -9
item.description: I ran Pi three ways (pi --print, the AI SDK's HarnessAgent, Cloudflare's PiHarness) and killed each mid-task. What came back, and why.

item.title: Pi + DeepSeek Flash, 169 merged PRs: 8–16¢ each
item.description: In model tokens at DeepSeek off-peak prices, 169 merged deliveries cost a median of $0.082 each. One issue through four Pi sessions; what Pi leaves out.

item.title: Claude Code headless mode exits 0 despite denials
item.description: In Claude Code headless mode, a claude -p run with denied tool calls still exits 0. Use --output-format json and check permission_denials to catch it.

item.title: Searching for Orbi's harness, part 2: guard cost
item.description: On eight unseen bugs whose Issue shows only a narrow example, Orbi's original harness failed a third of its runs. Five designs to cut the cost of the fix.

item.title: Searching for Orbi's harness, part 1: review gaps
item.description: Orbi's review passed two fixes that each broke something. We rebuilt the harness one rule at a time and reran the loop on failed and unseen issues.

item.title: GitSpawn and the agent that never asks
item.description: A git flaw hit seven coding agents by skipping their approval prompts. Orbi has none to skip, so we shipped a fix, checked who runs git, and reverted it.

item.title: DeepSeek coding agent cost per merged PR
item.description: See how Orbi uses DeepSeek as an unattended coding agent, what each merged PR costs, why cache reads matter, and how to connect your own API key.

item.title: Why Orbi is open source again
item.description: Orbi began on Apache-2.0 and switched to the Sustainable Use License on Sep 4. From v0.5.44 it is AGPL-3.0, or the SUL if AGPL is ruled out. Here is why.

item.title: The k8e etcd ticket that closed too early
item.description: Orbi wrote an etcd test suite for k8e, a 497-star Kubernetes distro. It was rejected, fixed and merged, and the four-phase issue closed after phase one.

item.title: How one slash command got its shape
item.description: A close look at the name, syntax, regex anchor, and registry behind one in-ticket command, compared with Prow and bors-ng and checked against their source.

item.title: The engine waited for an answer users could not give
item.description: Our engine paused for a human decision, then asked tenants to use a command they did not have. Three versions of the same mistake in one afternoon.

item.title: Seven steps of an Orbi Cloud setup, on video
item.description: An 83-second video follows the Orbi Cloud setup from GitHub sign-in to a tagged release and subscription. The final step starts paid Cloud delivery here.

item.title: What an autonomous coding agent does when it says no
item.description: Most autonomous coding agents stop at a pull request. Here, a second model rejected the diff twice, while the commits and release remain inspectable.

item.title: Claude Code in Actions: who presses merge?
item.description: Claude Code Action can implement and review pull requests in your runner. It stops before merge and release. Here is the evidence-backed layer for both.

item.title: The Docker image made it out on try three
item.description: The orbi image reached GHCR and Docker Hub on its third run. The first two failures were build context and Dockerfile paths; the last an invalid tag.
